name: Load Balancing & Consistent Hashing
tagline: Distributing network connections and RPCs across healthy backends using L4/L7 routing, P2C-EWMA, and consistent hashing.
purpose: Build a progressive mental model of load balancing—from L4 vs L7 trade-offs and the HTTP/2 multiplexing trap to Power of Two Choices (P2C) and outlier ejection.

spark.summary: Distributing incoming network connections or application requests across healthy backend servers to maximize throughput, minimize tail latency, and survive node failures seamlessly.
spark.keyTakeaway: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, match the balancing layer and algorithm to your traffic: use L4 (Maglev/DSR) for raw packet scale, L7 (Envoy/ALB) for gRPC/HTTP routing, and Power of Two Choices (P2C) + EWMA to crush tail latency.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **load balancer** distributes incoming connections or requests across a pool of backend servers while removing unhealthy instances from rotation: **L4 (Transport)**: routes on `(src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, proto)` using IPVS/eBPF/Maglev at >10M packets/sec.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Virtual-Node Hash Ring for Stateful Affinity & Cache Locality (N1 -> N2 -> N3 -> N4 -> N1a); Why gRPC Requires L7 or Client-Side Load Balancing (gRPC Client -> Envoy L7 Proxy -> Pod 1 (EWMA 4ms) -> Pod 2 (EWMA 22ms)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose between packet-rate scale, protocol intelligence, and zero-hop client routing. Hyperscale architectures combine an **L4 Maglev/ECMP edge** (horizontally scaling across BGP/Anycast IPs) in front of **L7 Envoy gateways** that terminate TLS, separate `/livez`.

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore gRPC HTTP/2 balancing, NGINX 502 buffer tuning, and consistent hashing.

learningJourney.title: What is Load Balancing (L4 vs L7 & Consistent Hashing)

explanation.foundation:
A **load balancer** distributes incoming connections or requests across a pool of backend servers while removing unhealthy instances from rotation:
- **L4 (Transport)**: routes on `(src_ip, src_port, dst_ip, dst_port, proto)` using IPVS/eBPF/Maglev at >10M packets/sec.
explanation.core: - **L7 (Application)**: terminates TLS/HTTP to inspect paths, headers, and gRPC frames.
explanation.deepDive: - **Consistent Hashing**: maps keys (`tenant_id`, `cache_key`) onto a hash ring with virtual nodes so adding/removing a backend only remaps $1/N$ keys.

sectionDiagram.title: Virtual-Node Hash Ring for Stateful Affinity & Cache Locality
sectionDiagram.summary: Virtual nodes (150–256 per physical host) prevent hot-spot skew and ensure only ~1/N keys move on scale-out.

learningJourney.title: Why Round Robin and L4-only fail on gRPC and heterogeneous workloads

explanation.foundation: Without load balancing, one overloaded instance or AZ outage takes down the service.
explanation.core:
Even with a balancer, two classic traps spike p99 latency:
- **The gRPC / HTTP/2 Trap**: HTTP/2 multiplexes thousands of RPCs over one long-lived TCP connection. An L4 balancer pins that single TCP connection to *one* backend pod forever.
explanation.deepDive: - **Health-Check Herd Collapse**: if one slow node fails `/healthz` and gets ejected, its load dumps onto the remaining nodes, knocking them out in a domino cascade.

sectionDiagram.summary: L7 proxies multiplex-unwrap HTTP/2 streams and use P2C+EWMA to steer RPCs away from degraded pods.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Load Balancing & Consistent Hashing without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, match the balancing layer and algorithm to your traffic: use L4 (Maglev/DSR) for raw packet scale, L7 (Envoy/ALB) for gRPC/HTTP routing, and Power of Two Choices (P2C) + EWMA to crush tail latency.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: Power of Two Choices (P2C) + Outlier & Slow-Start Config

explanation.foundation: Think of **Power of Two Choices (P2C) + Outlier & Slow-Start Config** as the intuition layer for Load Balancing & Consistent Hashing: Operational control: configure bounds, failure handling, and safe production defaults.
explanation.core: Envoy and Linkerd use **P2C + Peak EWMA**: sample 2 random backends and pick the one with lower active requests/latency. Pair this with `max_ejection_percent: 50` (panic threshold) and `slow_start_config` so newly booted pods warm caches gradually.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, power of two choices (p2c) + outlier & slow-start config becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Distributing incoming network connections or application requests across healthy backend servers to maximize throughput, minimize tail latency, and survive node failures seamlessly.

learningJourney.markdownContent:
```yaml
# Envoy Upstream Cluster: P2C + Outlier Ejection + Slow-Start
lb_policy: LEAST_REQUEST
least_request_lb_config:
  choice_count: 2
  slow_start_config:
    slow_start_window: 45s
outlier_detection:
  consecutive_5xx: 5
  interval: 10s
  base_ejection_time: 30s
  max_ejection_percent: 50  # Panic threshold prevents cascading domino ejection
```

knowledgeCheck.question: Why does an L4 TCP load balancer fail to distribute gRPC traffic evenly across newly scaled backend pods?

options.text: gRPC uses UDP instead of TCP
options.feedback: gRPC runs over HTTP/2 on top of TCP.

options.feedback: L4 balancers forward encrypted TCP packets transparently without terminating TLS.
